subject: computer-science
title: Databases: The Relational Model
welcome_lead: Tables, keys and relationships — the backbone of every business system.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: relations, primary and foreign keys, entity-relationship.
final_note: Get the model right and the queries follow.

concepts.def: A table of rows and columns in a relational database.
A single row in a relation.
An attribute (or set) uniquely identifying each tuple.
An attribute referencing the primary key of another relation.
A diagram of entities, attributes and relationships.

walkthroughs.body_html: The relational model (Codd, 1970) represents data as relations — sets of tuples with named attributes. Operations come from relational algebra (select, project, join).
A primary key uniquely identifies a row. A foreign key in one table references the primary key of another, enforcing referential integrity.
An ER diagram shows entities (boxes), attributes (ovals) and relationships (diamonds). Cardinality is annotated as 1:1, 1:M or M:N. M:N relationships need a junction table.
